requirement_text.REQ-365: Per explicit user decision: platform-level help (shared screens like login-routing that no tenant owns) is authored through the BA-agent/REQ-ANALYST pipeline, matching the exact platform-vs-tenant split already established for UAT scenarios (REQ-358's scope field, REQ-359's BA-persona/REQ-ANALYST split, REQ-360's login-routing scenario as the worked platform example). This requirement is the authoring-path equivalent for help content: it does not re-derive that split, it applies it. . SCOPE: wherever REQ-363's design placed platform-scope help content (a dedicated table/schema, per that requirement's own acceptance criterion), this requirement adds the write path/tooling REQ-ANALYST (or, once REQ-359 lands, whichever role it specifies for platform content) actually uses to author it — this could be as simple as a direct context-module call analogous to REQ-364's tenant-scoped one, scoped to the platform table instead, reusing REQ-364's create/update/publish/reconfirm shape rather than inventing a parallel one. Explicitly NOT a new UI — platform help authoring is agent-pipeline-driven, matching how platform-scope UAT scenarios are authored (a file/record written by an agent, not a form filled by a human). . FIRST REAL CONTENT: author help for the login-routing screen (the same screen REQ-360's UAT scenario covers) as this requirement's own worked, real example — proves the authoring path end-to-end rather than shipping an authoring mechanism with zero real content using it.

task.description: On branch feature/WF02-REQ365-20260918. Read lib/letflow/design/req365-platform-help-authoring.md independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Hard-gate it per WF-02 Step 1b (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md): every REQ-365 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferral language on anything in scope, function signatures fully specified (name/inputs/outputs/error cases), error-handling shape stated, cross-module dependencies listed, no implementation code (.ex bodies) present — signatures/type-shapes/literal content text only. Specifically verify: (a) the platform_help_content migration shape is fully specified and consistent with req363 design §3 (public schema, no prefix, no tenant_scoped_migrations registration); (b) the write-path module/function shapes are complete and consistent with lib/letflow/help.ex's actual shipped signatures (read that file, don't take the design doc's word for it); (c) the sanitization-reuse mechanism is concretely specified, not hand-waved; (d) the literal login-routing help content text is genuinely present, in plain end-user language, and the screen_id is stated explicitly. FAIL immediately on any check failure, no partial credit — list every failed check by requirement id. On PASS, complete the handoff (status COMPLETED, result.status PASS, next_action "Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a)"), commit and push to feature/WF02-REQ365-20260918. On FAIL, complete the handoff with result.status FAIL and next_action "Rework CODE-DESIGNER", listing every failed check.
